evidence: Flag is a false positive: 7358699 touches only sync_engine_race_test.go and sync_cadence.go, while the whole-unit retry comment in commit_lock.go was already in the round-0 code, which round 0 approved. The agent built the reviewer's second option, a resume-at-versioning phase marker.
guidance_note: When widening a retry boundary around a multi-step non-idempotent sequence, list every partial-success point (here tx.Commit succeeded, DOLT_COMMIT failed) and write down what the retry re-executes from each one before claiming the retry is safe.

evidence: 7358699 added runDolt(t, base, "clone", ...) and doltRefCommitCount, so the test now shells out to dolt and still guards only exec.LookPath("git"). caused_by is null because 7358699 was a commit after round 0's approval that fixed no review finding: round 0 had zero findings. guidance_note: When a test edit adds a call to a new external binary, add that binary's LookPath skip in the same edit, copying the sibling test's guards.

evidence: The mirror-spawn debounce (mirrorSpawnDebounceInterval = 1s) arrived in 7358699 with no changelog entry. evidence: Flag is a false positive: 8516a05 only adds dumpMirrorLog to the race test. This finding re-raises F1's double-apply defect, which was still unfixed at round 2 because the agent's replies came four days later (2026-08-14). The same 206b522 phase-marker fix closes it.

evidence: In 7358699, markMirrorSpawnAttempt sits inside `else if hasRemote`, so neither the remote-check error path nor the no-remote path stamps the marker. Every mutation in a burst therefore repeats the check and the stderr warning. caused_by is null because 7358699 fixed no finding. evidence: TestShouldReceiveNowDebounce already tests the shared primitive shouldRunNow through the shouldReceiveNow wrapper, so the claim that the primitives are untested overstates the gap. guidance_note: When adding a second instance of a shared primitive, extend the existing instance's test to cover the new marker and its independence from the first.

evidence: This re-raises F3 (the debounce missing from the changelog), which was unaddressed at round 2. Flag is a false positive: 8516a05 touches only test diagnostics. The 2293e3e Changed entry resolves it.

narrative: Round 0 approved the PR and missed a real double-apply bug in the widened withMutation retry. The agent then pushed post-approval flake work (7358699), which added the mirror-spawn debounce and a dolt oracle with no changelog entry, no dolt skip guard and incomplete marker stamping. Round 1 caught those plus the retry bug. Round 2 followed a diagnostics-only push and re-raised the unaddressed findings. No finding was caused by a fix for another finding. The agent answered everything four days later in 2293e3e and 206b522 and proved the double-apply bug with a regression test.
guidance_observations: The round-0 approval was wrong: the whole-unit retry comment claimed safety the code did not have. An approval is not evidence the code is correct.
Scope added after approval (the debounce) came with no changelog entry and no unit test, which is what produced most of rounds 1 and 2.
Findings stayed unanswered while the agent pushed further commits, so round 2 spent half its findings re-raising round 1.

evidence: The cold-start sentence ('behaves exactly as before') appears in the hunk, but the bottom-of-frame placement text at lines 338-340 that would contradict it does not, so the packet cannot settle the contradiction. evidence: The invariant reads 'Only opaque discriminators enter the shared database'. Lines later the doc floats a user-chosen label for 'friendlier remote rendering', which would have to sync. The label is only a future nicety, not adopted, so the reviewer overstates it, but a reader still cannot tell whether the invariant allows an exception. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: Before calling a design doc accepted, check every absolute claim in it ('exactly as before', 'only', 'never') against each behavior change the same doc accepts.

evidence: Step 1 reads 'a dependency outside the claimed lane that gates it is on the path and is offered', with no claim-status qualifier. Step 4 says lanes claimed elsewhere are skipped, and the step-2 example writes the qualifier ('E.4 (unclaimed, on your path)') that step 1 leaves out. The spec is self-inconsistent. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When writing a precedence list, run each rule against every other rule's case (claimed-elsewhere, stale, unclaimed) and write down the result.

evidence: The doc says 'A claim ends three ways, none of them a command', but its own predicate says 'Only ticket lifecycle transitions establish or transfer a claim', and step 5 describes a takeover by starting a ticket. Transfer is therefore a fourth ending, and a command triggers it. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When a doc enumerates 'N ways' something happens, grep the same doc for every verb that does it (transfer, takeover) and reconcile the count.

evidence: The design lists 'liveness' as a derived state and defines a local liveness prune by enumerating worktrees, so 'only staleness heuristics' is inaccurate. The sentence is really ruling out heartbeats and process probes, which is narrower than the reviewer reads it. A one-word scoping fix was warranted. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: Before calling a design doc accepted, check every absolute claim in it ('exactly as before', 'only', 'never') against each behavior change the same doc accepts.

evidence: The state inventory says 'Shared, synchronized: work records ... Nothing else is added' and 'Local: one write-once stream-id token', but T is 'per-repository configurable' and drives every claim derivation. Where T lives, and whether it syncs, is unstated. Two checkouts with different T values would derive different claims. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When a design includes a state inventory, place every configurable parameter that feeds a derivation in it as well.

evidence: The new Status says a doc/behavior divergence is 'not an automatic win for either', while the archive README (quoted by the reviewer) says 'the code wins'. The two give opposite resolution rules, and the README index entry added in this PR does not reconcile them. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When adding a doc to an archive that has stated rules (here 'code wins'), read the archive's README rules and either conform to them or amend them in the same PR.

evidence: The README says each doc carries its own Status header, yet the new index entry repeats '*Accepted design.*'. None of the neighboring entries in the hunk annotate status. The duplication is minor but real, and the fix is to drop it. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When adding an index entry, match the format of the existing entries and do not restate fields the target doc owns.

evidence: Step 2 says completing the last ticket 'announces the epic's completion' and the checkout 'is global again'. The granularity section says multi-lane epics are 'claimable lane by lane', so finishing one lane does not finish the epic. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When the doc changes its unit (epic to lane), sweep every later sentence that still names the old unit.

evidence: The claim depends on agent-identity-and-ownership.md's Status: draft and its actual thesis wording, and that doc is not in the packet. The review was posted after merge.

'Stale' is defined as 'The lane is unclaimed again', step 3 serves 'the top-ranked ready ticket in unclaimed lanes', and step 5 says stale lanes are 'never reached by bare next'. As written, bare next serves stale lanes. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When writing a precedence list, run each rule against every other rule's case (claimed-elsewhere, stale, unclaimed) and write down the result.

evidence: The stream id is specified only as 'a short opaque token', with no uniqueness requirement, yet contest detection depends on it being unique. A random collision is overstated as a risk, but a copied or restored token file is a real way to merge two claimants. One sentence requiring the token to be unique would close it. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When a design names an identity primitive, state its uniqueness requirement and how it is generated in the same paragraph.

narrative: This design-doc PR merged at 06:56Z, 15 minutes after it was opened. The CHANGES_REQUESTED review arrived at 07:26Z, after the merge, so none of its 12 findings got a reply. Most findings are real internal contradictions in work-claims.md: routing precedence (stale lanes, claimed-elsewhere dependencies), the 'three ways' a claim ends, epic versus lane completion, and the parameter T missing from the state inventory. They shipped in a document marked as an accepted design.
guidance_observations: The merge did not wait for the review, so an accepted design shipped with unanswered CHANGES_REQUESTED findings.
One self-consistency pass, checking every absolute or enumerated claim against the rest of the doc, would have caught most of the 12 findings before review.

evidence: maybeNotifyOwner calls ownerNotifyDue, runs the hook for up to 10s, and only then calls writeMarkerAtomic. Two detectors running at the same time (a foreground command and the detached mirror, which the doc comment itself names as concurrent writers) can both pass the check and both notify. The PR merged at 20:03Z, before the review at 00:29Z.
guidance_note: When a dedupe marker guards a slow side effect and the code already names concurrent writers, claim the marker atomically (O_EXCL or flock) before the side effect, not after it.

evidence: exec.CommandContext(hookCtx, "sh", "-c", hook) with CombinedOutput kills only sh on timeout. A background descendant that holds the inherited pipe makes Wait block past the deadline unless cmd.WaitDelay is set or the process group is killed. The comment's 'time-boxed' promise therefore does not hold. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When time-boxing a user-supplied shell command, set cmd.WaitDelay or kill the process group, and test the timeout with a hook that backgrounds a child.

evidence: The hunk shows reconcile still returning MergeConflictError for held prose, and that line is unchanged context. The packet does not show the pull path returning SyncFailureError or how commandErrorReason maps each error, so the claimed mismatch cannot be confirmed here. The review was posted after merge.

ownerNotifyMarkerPath is keyed by kind only, while fingerprint() includes ev.Remote + "/" + ev.Branch. Two episodes of the same kind on different targets therefore overwrite each other's marker, and clearing one target erases the other's. This is narrow in practice with one sync remote, but real. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When the dedupe identity (fingerprint) is finer than the storage key, key storage by the fingerprint, or clear only on a fingerprint match.

evidence: OwnerNotifyCmd is a SyncConfig field that the shared loader reads, and the reviewer says it reads it from the project layer at <workspace>/.lit/config.toml. The value then runs through sh -c. If that file is tracked, a cloned repo can ship a command that runs on the user's machine. The packet does not show whether .lit/config.toml is committed, but the field lets the project layer set it. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When adding a config key that is executed as a command, restrict it to the user-owned global config layer, as git does for hooks.

evidence: This duplicates F1 (check, then hook, then write is not atomic). It adds a real second case: a clearOwnerNotify that lands during a slow hook is overwritten by the later marker write, which suppresses the next episode. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When a dedupe marker guards a slow side effect and the code already names concurrent writers, claim the marker atomically (O_EXCL or flock) before the side effect, not after it.

evidence: This duplicates F1 and F4 together: markers keyed per kind collide across remotes, and the due-check is not atomic. Both are visible in ownerNotifyMarkerPath and maybeNotifyOwner. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When the dedupe identity (fingerprint) is finer than the storage key, key storage by the fingerprint, or clear only on a fingerprint match.

evidence: This duplicates F2: CommandContext kills only sh, a grandchild holds the pipe, and CombinedOutput outlives ownerNotifyHookTimeout. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When time-boxing a user-supplied shell command, set cmd.WaitDelay or kill the process group, and test the timeout with a hook that backgrounds a child.

evidence: The helper's code is `_, acquired, err := store.TryAcquireSyncPushLock(...)`, which discards the release closure. Its comment relies on the kernel holding the flock until the process exits. Go's os.File finalizer closes an unreachable fd, which releases the flock early and reopens the race the helper exists to close. The packet does not show acquireFileLock keeping another reference to the file. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When a correctness argument rests on a lock being held 'until process exit', keep the handle reachable explicitly, for example in a package-level variable, rather than discarding it.

evidence: This is a third report of the F2 hook-timeout defect, at a different line. The mechanism is the same: no WaitDelay and no process-group kill. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When time-boxing a user-supplied shell command, set cmd.WaitDelay or kill the process group, and test the timeout with a hook that backgrounds a child.

evidence: This is a third report of the F1/F6 dedupe race, including the case where a clear is overwritten by a marker written later. The code path is the same: ownerNotifyDue, then the hook, then writeMarkerAtomic. The review was posted after merge.
guidance_note: When a dedupe marker guards a slow side effect and the code already names concurrent writers, claim the marker atomically (O_EXCL or flock) before the side effect, not after it.

evidence: The syncTraceRecord literals in the hunk set Command, Decision, Status, Reason, BuildNote and Metadata, with no actor or session field. The doc's claim that the traces show 'who claimed that authority' is therefore unsupported by anything visible. The review was posted after merge.

narrative: The PR merged at 20:03Z, 32 minutes after it was opened. The CHANGES_REQUESTED review came at 00:29Z the next day, so none of its 13 findings got a reply. Three real defects shipped: a check-then-act dedupe race, a hook timeout that a backgrounded child can escape, and a project-config shell command (a security concern). Two smaller ones shipped too: per-kind markers that collide across remotes, and a discarded flock handle in a test. The review reported the race three times and the timeout three times.
guidance_observations: The merge did not wait for the review, so a reported security issue and two concurrency defects merged without being triaged.
The code's own comments named the concurrent writers (a foreground command and the detached mirror) and promised a time box, but neither claim was tested.
